about.text: Hungary’s soured cream, bone-white, thick and pourable: by the Hungarian food code, cream made from milk with added cream or butter, homogenised and set by a pure culture of lactic acid bacteria.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Industrial tejföl is cream heated to 75 °C, homogenised at 100-160 bar so that it does not separate, and set with a lactic culture, either in the cup or in a tank. Fermentation temperature and time are not given by the source. The article is inconsistent on the minimum fat (10, 12 and 16 % all appear).

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: At 100–160 bar, so that it does not separate.
Set with a lactic culture, in the cup (firm tejföl) or in the tank and then stirred (smooth, habart tejföl).

processing.text: Industrially set with a pure lactic culture, in the cup or in a tank. Traditionally the cream rose on warm milk for 2-3 days in summer, 6-7 in winter, and soured by itself.

facts.v: Usually 12 % and 20 %, less often 10 % or 16 %; the fat must be on the label
May keep the name if the treatment is stated
